name: Hugging pose
blurb: Arms around a plush, a pillow, a pet or another person: soft, warm and cosy
title: Hugging Pose Reference: Hugging a Plush, Pillow or Another Person
description: Hugging pose reference: hugging a plush, pillow or friend, how arms wrap and squash in a drawing, and how to pose a cosy hug for portrait photos.
answer: A hugging pose wraps the arms around something, such as a stuffed toy, pillow, pet or another person, and usually pulls it close to the chest. It reads as warm, comforting or shy, and the squeeze of the arms against the object is what makes it convincing.

body: Holding something soft gives the hands a natural job, which removes the biggest problem in portrait posing: what to do with the arms. It also adds a prop that can carry colour and character, from a big plush in pyjama shots to a pet in a lifestyle photo.
A hug pulls the shoulders forward and lowers the chin, so the pose feels protective and gentle. With two people it shows closeness without needing much facial expression.

ul: Plush hug: a stuffed toy held against the chest, chin resting on its head.
Pillow hug: a cushion squeezed in front, often while sitting or lying.
Peek over: only the eyes and forehead show above the plush.
Side hug: one arm around a friend's shoulders, both facing the camera.
Back hug: one person wraps the arms around the other from behind.
Face-to-face hug: arms around each other, heads turned on opposite sides.

body: Curve the line of action forward around the object, since a hug rounds the back and brings the shoulders in. Draw the object being hugged as a simple volume, then wrap the arms around it as tubes that disappear behind it. Wherever an arm presses in, dent the object's outline and bulge it out on either side; that squash is what makes the grip look real.

Hands usually end up partly hidden, with fingers spread across the back of the plush or the other person. The forearms and upper arms overlap, so check that each arm still has believable length. In two-person hugs, sketch both skeletons first so the shoulders and heads do not collide.

sections.h: How to pose and photograph a hugging pose
body: Shoot at or slightly above eye level, close enough that the prop and face fill the frame. A soft window light suits the mood. Ask the subject to squeeze the prop a little rather than just hold it, so the arms and the fabric show tension.

ul: Choose a prop roughly torso-sized; tiny props get lost and giant ones hide the face.
Tilt the head onto the plush or partner and keep the eyes toward the lens or closed.
For pairs, overlap the bodies slightly and let the taller person lower their shoulder.

faq.q: How do I draw arms wrapped around something?
faq.a: Draw the object as a solid shape first, then curve the arms around it as cylinders that overlap and press in, denting the outline where they squeeze.

faq.q: What can I hug in a photo if I have no plush?
faq.a: A pillow, a folded blanket, a jacket, a bouquet or a pet all work; anything soft that is easy to squeeze.

faq.q: Which pose shows closeness between two people?
faq.a: A side hug for casual friends, a back hug or face-to-face hug for close relationships.
